songs.name: Sitting On Top Of The World

ai_show_review.summary: Epic Smokestack opener, massive Lovelight jam, tight St. Stephen sandwich
ai_show_review.blurb: The set kicks off with a thunderous Smokestack Lightning and flows into the classic early‑70 Saint Stephen > Not Fade Away > Saint Stephen sandwich. Highlights include an adventurous Dark Star, a 35‑minute Turn On Your Lovelight, and inspired performances from Garcia and Weir. The composite matrix source captures the full show despite a slightly tinny mix and low‑sitting drums.
ai_show_review.review:
On February 8, 1970 at the Fillmore West the Dead delivered an early‑70 powerhouse that still shines for modern ears. A blistering Smokestack Lightning opens the night, with Garcia’s lead cutting through the foggy ambience and a fierce guitar duel with Bob Weir that reviewers call a high point. The first set rolls through Morning Dew, Dire Wolf, Me And My Uncle, Sitting On Top Of The World and the bright China Cat Sunflower → I Know You Rider segue before slipping into a soulful It Hurts Me Too. 

The second set launches with an exploratory Dark Star that builds into a rare Saint Stephen → Not Fade Away → Saint Stephen sandwich, then erupts into a monumental 35‑minute Turn On Your Lovelight jam that carries the band to a euphoric close. Garcia’s tone is described as “perfect” on Smokestack and chiming on China Cat, while Weir’s rhythm work and vocal interplay keep the momentum tight. Although the drums sit low in the mix, the overall playing is solid and the composite matrix recording captures the full arc of the performance better than any single audience tape.

best_recording.reason: Composite matrix source captures the entire show with clearer board audio after the mid‑show switch, delivering the best overall balance despite a slightly tinny mix and low drums.

key_highlights: Thunderous Smokestack Lightning opener sets a high bar
35‑minute Turn On Your Lovelight jam showcases expansive improvisation
Adventurous Dark Star early in the second set
Rare Saint Stephen > Not Fade Away > Saint Stephen sandwich adds intrigue

band_performance.Jerry: Garcia delivers a perfect tone on Smokestack, chiming leads in China Cat Sunflower, digs deep during Not Fade Away and drives the marathon Lovelight jam; his duel with Bob on Smokestack is repeatedly praised.
band_performance.Bob: Weir’s rhythm work and vocal interplay shine throughout, especially in the early set and the St. Stephen sandwich; his guitar duel with Jerry on Smokestack is a highlight, though his vocal scream during St. Stephen is noted as chaotic.
